headingScale.note: measured — no bare h1/h2/h3/h4 element rule sets a size; sizes are applied through the named .text-heading-N utility scale and per-component rules, so tag-to-size mapping is not determinable from CSS alone

selectorEvidence: measured — 14px is the single most-declared font-size across all fetched stylesheets (34 declarations); 20px is the most-declared line-height (32 declarations)
measured — root sizing: `:root,:host { font-size:16px; line-height:1.5rem }` and `body { font-size:100% }` (Tailwind preflight); `footer { font-size:14px }` in page markup
measured — .text-copy-16 { font-size:16px; line-height:24px } is the next step and is used for larger prose
bodyCandidates.caveat: the exact size applied to docs prose paragraphs cannot be confirmed statically because the utility class is chosen per element; 14/20 is the dominant declared pairing, 16/24 the second

fluidType.evidence: measured — clamp() appears in font-size declarations, e.g. `--font-size: clamp(12px, var(--computed-font-size), 32px)` (and 16/48, 24/64, 24/72 variants) and `.djIg-q_step h3 { font-size: clamp(1rem,4vw,1.2rem) }`
fluidType.scope: confined to a few display/marketing components; the docs type scale itself is fixed-px, not fluid

namedTypeScale.source: measured — compiled Tailwind utility classes .text-heading-N / .text-copy-N / .text-label-N in the fetched stylesheets

spacing.evidence: measured — literal lengths in margin/padding/gap/inset declarations across all 8 fetched stylesheets plus the 2 inline blocks; rem converted at the declared 16px root. 84.5% of weighted literal lengths are multiples of 4px; 61.2% are multiples of 8px, so 4px is the base and 8px the common step. 1px and 2px occur only as hairline borders/offsets.

backgroundCandidate.declaration: body { background: var(--geist-background) }; surfaces use var(--ds-background-100)

contrastRatioCandidate.method: WCAG 2.x relative-luminance ratio computed from the resolved plain hex token values; the sRGB branch is used (the site also restates these in lab() under @media (color-gamut:p3), which was not used for the ratio)

darkModeEvidence.primary: measured — theme tokens are redefined under the selector list `.dark, .dark-theme, .invert-theme` and `[data-theme=dark]`; light values sit on `:root, .light-theme, .dark .invert-theme, .dark-theme .invert-theme`
darkModeEvidence.prefersColorSchemeRole: measured — the single @media (prefers-color-scheme:dark) block only carries compiled Tailwind `dark:` utility variants, not the token definitions; it is a secondary path, not the mechanism
darkModeEvidence.serverRenderedRootClass: measured — the delivered <html> element carries font/variable classes and `tailwind tailwind-preflight`, but no dark/light class, so the theme class is applied client-side (localStorage referenced twice in the payload)
darkModeEvidence.p3Widening: measured — 4 @media (color-gamut:p3) blocks redefine tokens in lab() for wide-gamut displays

color.tokenNaming: measured — two coexisting families: legacy `--geist-*` and current `--ds-*` (e.g. --ds-gray-100…1000, --ds-background-100/200, --ds-gray-alpha-*), a 100–1000 numeric ramp rather than named shades
color.customPropertySelection: measured — the 80 shown are plain-colour tokens resolved per theme, ordered gray ramp, background ramp, gray-alpha ramp, hue ramps, then legacy --geist-*. 168 plain-colour tokens were found in total, out of 660 custom properties overall; shadow, gradient and non-colour tokens are excluded from this list.
color.rampShape: measured — the neutral ramp is --ds-gray-100 … --ds-gray-1000 plus --ds-gray-alpha-100 … --ds-gray-alpha-1000 (translucent twins for overlaying), with surfaces on --ds-background-100/200. Light and dark are mirrored rather than merely inverted: --ds-gray-1000 is #171717 on #fff (17.93:1) and #ededed on #000 (17.94:1), so the two themes carry the same contrast budget.

selectorEvidence: aside … w-[240px] max-w-[240px] sticky top-[var(--docs-content-sticky-top)] hidden lg:block

gridUsage.note: measured — flex dominates (137 display:flex declarations vs 20 display:grid). Grid is used for the docs shell columns (grid-cols-[300px_1fr]) and card decks (repeat(N,minmax(0,1fr)), repeat(auto-fit,minmax(300px,1fr))).

derivedProseColumn.note: measured inputs, not a measured value — the reading column is the 1448px frame minus a 300px left sidebar and a 240px right rail plus gutters (~24px each). No single max-width rule governs it, so the rendered prose width is not determinable statically; it would need a computed-style read at a known viewport.

layout.primaryBreakpointFamily: measured — the site runs two overlapping systems: a Geist set at 401 / 601 / 951 / 961 / 1200 / 1400 px and a Tailwind set at 640 / 768 / 1024 / 1280 px; 601/600 is by far the most used pair (28 min + 16 max), then 961/960, then 401. The docs shell itself switches at Tailwind `lg` (1024px) for the sidebar and rail, and at 880px for the top nav.

behaviours.name: scroll-spy on the on-this-page rail
behaviours.evidence: weak — 34 aria-current attributes and a sticky 240px rail imply a highlighted current section, but no IntersectionObserver string is present in the delivered markup, so the mechanism is not confirmed.

measurement.method: curl with a desktop Chrome user-agent, --compressed, -L, 20s timeout; both pages returned HTTP 200 on the first attempt with no challenge. 8 linked stylesheets fetched (all 200) plus 2 inline <style> blocks extracted. All figures derived with node/grep over the saved files.
notes: Not blocked and not a JS-only shell: /docs/functions delivers 37,261 characters of visible text server-side and /docs delivers 10,276 — well above the 500-character threshold, so the docs prose is in the HTML.
Text-to-HTML ratio is very low (1.2% and 3.1%) because the pages are Next.js App Router RSC payloads: most bytes are serialized flight data and Tailwind class strings, not markup overhead.

Every value above is measured from delivered markup or fetched CSS, or explicitly labelled inferred (DOM/script presence). No computed styles were read and no browser was run, so anything requiring layout — the rendered prose column width, which utility class lands on a given paragraph, whether a handler actually fires — is recorded as null or caveated rather than guessed.
Font files were not fetched. GeistSans / Geist Mono are named in --font-geist-sans and --font-mono with declared fallback stacks.
Stylesheet byte counts are the decompressed sizes on disk; the wire transfer was smaller (e.g. the 452,789-byte main chunk transferred as 75,077 bytes gzipped).
Nothing was copied into the repository: raw HTML and CSS live only under data/design-study/raw/vercel_com_docs/ which is gitignored.

measured.method: Chromium computed styles via javascript_tool. Desktop emulated at 1440x900 (the pane's own 'desktop' preset reports a 0x0 viewport); mobile at the 375x812 preset with a reload. Characters per line = paragraph content-box width / average glyph width of a 100-character lorem span in the paragraph's exact computed font styles.

assignedUrlIsNotAReadingPage.finding: The docs landing page holds one paragraph over 40 characters (713 characters of card blurb in a container with class 'relative overflow-hidden max-h-12' — a line-clamped card description). Its 990px width and 154 characters per line describe a card grid, not a reading measure.
